qti-assessment-test.title: ATrain Education - Suicide Screening, Imminent Harm Referral & Acetaminophen Safety (ANCC NCPD Self-Study Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Differentiate imminent suicide harm protocols from moderate-risk outpatient safety planning.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Differentiate imminent suicide harm protocols from moderate-risk outpatient safety planning.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During an outpatient nursing triage visit, a 42-year-old patient endorses active suicidal ideation with a specific plan tonight and reports having an unlocked firearm at home. Which action satisfies ANCC evidence-based imminent-harm referral standards?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Maintain continuous staff observation, initiate immediate emergency psychiatric evaluation and lethal-means restriction with family support, and document a warm clinical handoff.
Provide the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline wallet card, schedule a 72-hour telehealth follow-up, and discharge the patient home alone after verbal reassurance.
Defer formal risk documentation until the next scheduled primary-care visit to avoid triggering involuntary-hold anxiety.
Ask the patient to mail the firearm key to the clinic within five business days and complete a self-guided mood diary.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Active suicidal intent with a specific plan and accessible lethal means requires continuous observation, immediate emergency evaluation, and documented warm transfer rather than unsupervised discharge.
Incorrect. Verbal 'no-harm' reassurance does not mitigate imminent risk when an active plan and lethal means are present.
Incorrect. Delaying documentation and crisis intervention violates clinical duty-of-care and state suicide-screening mandates.
Incorrect. Delayed self-managed lethal-means steps leave acute tonight-level risk unaddressed.

qti-assessment-item.title: Calculate cumulative 24-hour acetaminophen exposure across prescription and OTC products.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Calculate cumulative 24-hour acetaminophen exposure across prescription and OTC products.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A post-operative patient takes two hydrocodone/acetaminophen 5 mg/325 mg tablets every 6 hours (4 doses in 24 hours) and also takes two extra-strength OTC cold caplets containing 500 mg acetaminophen each every 6 hours (4 doses in 24 hours). What is the patient's total 24-hour acetaminophen intake and required nursing action?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: 6,600 mg/24 hours; hold further acetaminophen-containing doses immediately, notify the prescriber, and assess hepatic function and staggered-overdose risk.
3,600 mg/24 hours; continue both medications as scheduled because prescription tablets are capped at 325 mg per tablet.
6,600 mg/24 hours; wait for a single 4-hour Rumack-Matthew nomogram plot before contacting the prescriber.
4,000 mg/24 hours; instruct the patient to double fluid intake while keeping both regimens unchanged.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Four PRN doses of 650 mg equal 2,600 mg plus four OTC doses of 1,000 mg equal 4,000 mg, totaling 6,600 mg/day - well above the 4,000 mg/day adult ceiling.
Incorrect. Counting only single tablets instead of two-tablet doses undercounts total intake by nearly half and overlooks hepatotoxic stacking.
Incorrect. The Rumack-Matthew nomogram applies only to single acute ingestions at a known time, not staggered supratherapeutic dosing over 24 hours.
Incorrect. Hydration neither reduces glutathione-depleting NAPQI metabolite formation nor corrects a 6,600 mg/day supratherapeutic dose.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply N-acetylcysteine (NAC) hepatoprotective window principles in acute acetaminophen toxicity.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply N-acetylcysteine (NAC) hepatoprotective window principles in acute acetaminophen toxicity.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: When a patient presents after a confirmed single acute toxic acetaminophen ingestion, why do clinical guidelines prioritize initiating N-acetylcysteine (NAC) within 8 hours of ingestion?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: NAC replenishes hepatic glutathione stores to detoxify NAPQI before irreversible centrilobular hepatocyte necrosis occurs, achieving near-complete hepatoprotection within 8 hours.
NAC competitively blocks gastrointestinal absorption of intact acetaminophen tablets in the stomach lumen.
NAC is ineffective once 8 hours have elapsed and must never be started if serum transaminases have begun rising.
NAC alkalinizes renal tubular urine to accelerate unchanged parent-drug excretion.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Administering NAC within 8 hours restores hepatic glutathione to conjugate toxic NAPQI metabolites before severe hepatocellular injury develops.
Incorrect. Activated charcoal reduces early GI absorption, whereas NAC acts systemically as a glutathione precursor and sulfhydryl donor.
Incorrect. While efficacy peaks within 8 hours, NAC still reduces mortality and hepatic failure in late presentations and elevated-transaminase cases.
Incorrect. Urinary alkalinization treats salicylate toxicity, not acetaminophen NAPQI hepatotoxicity.
